body.statement: The answer is affirmative for post-summary computation.  Let \(Q=8(n^2+2n)\).  For outward rational enclosures of the exact fixed-coordinate empirical covariance summaries, refined to the selected working precision, and, when an ambient encoder is requested, an outward rational enclosure of \(U\), all of total input length \(L\), the capped procedure \(\mathsf C_{\mathbb Q}\) assigns at most \(e_{\star}/(4Q)\) arithmetic enclosure error to each reached operation, has total arithmetic enclosure error at most \(e_{\star}/4\) within every restarted transcript, and certifies every inverse, rank, zero-versus-positive spectral split, repeated invariant subspace, projector product, and largest-singular-value comparison used by \(\mathsf C\).  On every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa)\), it terminates on every input by the cap \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}\), returning either \(\bot\) or a finite answer, and with probability at least \(1-\alpha\) it returns a non-abstaining answer satisfying \(\widehat{\mathcal G}=I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widehat H,P)\le\tau\).  With logarithms of reciprocals truncated below at zero, its working precision and post-summary Boolean running time are polynomial in \(L,n,\log\kappa,\log(1/g_0),\log(1/h_0),\log(1/\alpha),\log(1/\tau)\).  No separation among repeated positive eigenvalues is required.  If computation begins from the raw streams rather than their summaries, reading and summarizing the data incurs in addition at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) input-record operations; thus no end-to-end running-time claim polynomial only in logarithmic gap parameters is made.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(Q=8(n^2+2n)\) and \(\beta=e_{\star}/(4Q)\).  In any one restarted transcript, the public program has \(n^2+2n-2\) reached matrix occurrences.  Adding \(n+1\) covariance inversions, \(n\) primitive formations, at most two projector constructions and one product-norm computation per graph comparison, and \(n\) singleton selections is bounded by \(Q\).  Assign the \(j\)-th operation in that restart a numerical enclosure radius
\[
 \varepsilon_j\le\beta,
 \tag{28}
\]
and, for the operation's own decision, reduce it further to the minimum of \(\beta\) and the required fixed fraction of \(g_0\), \(h_0\), \(1/\sqrt n\), or \(\tau/n\).  Then, deterministically,
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^{Q}\varepsilon_j\le Q\beta=e_{\star}/4.
 \tag{29}
\]

We first justify rational covariance algebra.  Clear denominators in an input covariance matrix.  Its integer entries have bit length at most \(O(L)\).  The Leibniz determinant formula has at most \(n!\) products of \(n\) such entries, so every determinant minor has bit length \(O(n(L+\log n))\).  Fraction-free elimination therefore decides positive definiteness and, when the matrix is invertible, computes its adjugate-over-determinant inverse with polynomially many operations on polynomial-bit integers.  Sums and the three-factor primitive formula increase numerator and denominator lengths only polynomially in \(L\) and \(n\).  Outward rounding every entry to \(p\) fractional bits gives operator error at most \(n2^{-p}\), because the operator norm is at most the Frobenius norm.  The min--max formula and the quadratic-form bound used in (9) transfer this operator radius to every ordered eigenvalue.  Thus primitive and eigenvalue enclosure error at most any prescribed \(\xi>0\) is obtained with
\[
 p=O\!\left(L+\log n+\log(1/\xi)\right).
 \tag{30}
\]
This contains, and sharpens for exact rational centers, the prior covariance-to-primitive partial result.  If the input itself is an outward interval rather than an exact rational center, the condition \(\lambda_{\min}(S_{m,r})\ge(2\kappa)^{-1}\) and the resolvent identity give the previously established additional inverse error \(4\kappa^2n2^{-p}\), and the primitive error is at most \(Cn\kappa^4 2^{-p}\); adding \(O(\log\kappa)\) bits in (30) absorbs it.

The nonalgebraic radius terms also have certified rational enclosures at polynomial cost.  A square root of a nonnegative rational is bracketed by bisection, and range reduction writes a positive rational as \(2^jy\) with \(y\in[1,2)\).  With \(z=(y-1)/(y+1)\in[0,1/3]\),
\[
 \log y=2\sum_{\ell=0}^{s}\frac{z^{2\ell+1}}{2\ell+1}+r_s,
 \qquad
 0\le r_s\le\frac{2z^{2s+3}}{(2s+3)(1-z^2)}.
\]
The same series at \(z=1/3\) encloses \(\log2\).  Thus \(O(p+L)\) rational terms suffice for \(p\) output bits, with explicit tail sign and magnitude; outward rounding gives certified values of \(t_r\) and \(a_r\) in polynomial Boolean time.

Rank certification does not require eigenvectors.  For a rational symmetric matrix \(K\) and rational \(x\), exact fraction-free symmetric elimination gives a rational block \(LDL^{\top}\) congruence of \(K-xI\).  Congruence preserves the maximal dimensions of positive and negative quadratic-form subspaces, so the signs of the one- and two-dimensional diagonal blocks determine the inertia and hence the number of eigenvalues below \(x\).  Bisection between rational endpoints gives outward eigenvalue intervals of width \(\xi\) in \(O(\log((1+\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}})/\xi))\) inertia calls.  The determinant-minor bound above proves polynomial bit growth in every call.  At the terminal stage, (18)--(19) from Theorem 1 give, for every reached \(M\),
\[
 b_M\le ne_{r_B}<g_0/112.
 \tag{31}
\]
Choosing the rational rounding radius below \(g_0/112\), the inertia counts certify that every empirical eigenvalue lies either in the zero cluster below \(g_0/28\) or in the positive cluster above \(27g_0/28\).  They consequently certify the population rank and the public forbidden band.  On an off-promise input, failure of these inequalities produces \(\bot\), not a rounded rank.

It remains to obtain whole invariant subspaces without separating eigenvalues inside a cluster.  At a certified occurrence let \(k\) be the inertia count of the empirical zero cluster.  If \(k=0\) or \(k=n\), the relevant projector is exactly \(I_n\) or \(0\).  Otherwise the only gap used is
\[
 \widehat\lambda_{k+1}-\widehat\lambda_k
 \ge g_0-2b_M>g_0/2.
 \tag{32}
\]
Moreover, when \(a_r\le(2\kappa)^{-1}\),
\[
 \|S_{m,r}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\kappa,
 \quad
 \|S_{0,r}^{-1}-S_{m,r}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le4\kappa,
 \quad
 \|\widehat R_r(M)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le24n\kappa^3.
 \tag{33}
\]
For a nonempty promised class, every singleton is nonzero by the variance reset and \(\|R_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le4\kappa^3\), so \(g_0\le4\kappa^3\).  Let \(K_0\) be the least power of two not smaller than \(32n\kappa^3\), so \(K_0<64n\kappa^3\).  Scale \(\widehat R_r(M)-g_0I_n/2\) by \(K_0\).  Its norm is at most one and its separating gap is at least \(g_0/(128n\kappa^3)\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certified\mbox{-}hermitian\mbox{-}projector}\), with \(S=I_n\), computes the projector onto the entire lower cluster to operator error \(\delta\) in Boolean time polynomial in
\[
 n,\quad \log\kappa,\quad \log(1/g_0),\quad \log(1/\delta).
 \tag{34}
\]
This invocation remains valid when eigenvalues are repeated within either cluster, because (32), not an internal eigengap, is its premise.  Converting rational entries to directed dyadics first changes the matrix by at most \(n2^{-p}\).  Projecting the perturbed invariant-subspace equation across the gap in (32), exactly as in (10), adds at most \(4n2^{-p}/g_0\) to the projector radius.  Choosing \(p\) from (30) absorbs this term into \(\delta\).

Let \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) be the two exact empirical positive-range projectors in a graph comparison, and let \(\widetilde P_1,\widetilde P_2\) be rational approximations with operator errors at most \(\delta\).  Outward-rounded multiplication gives
\[
 \|\widetilde P_1(I-\widetilde P_2)-P_1(I-P_2)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le2\delta+\delta^2+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mult}}.
 \tag{35}
\]
Choose the three local radii so that the right-hand side is at most \(\min\{\beta,h_0/16\}\).  For a rational matrix \(D\), the Hermitian dilation
\[
 \mathcal H(D)=
 \begin{pmatrix}0&D\\D^{\top}&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
has largest eigenvalue \(\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Exact rational inertia of \(\mathcal H(D)-xI\), followed by bisection, therefore encloses that largest singular value to any additive \(\xi\) with polynomially many polynomial-bit operations.  The norm is one-Lipschitz, so enlarging this interval by the right-hand side of (35) certifies the exact empirical projector-product norm.  By (19), its statistical distance from the population comparison is less than \(h_0/28\).  Taking \(\xi\le h_0/16\) leaves total distance less than \(h_0/4\), which separates \(0\) from \([h_0,1]\).  The path induction of Theorem 1 then proves that all finite-precision rank and graph decisions equal those of \(\mathsf C\).

For the encoder, let \(\widehat P_m\) be a nonzero empirical singleton projector and let \(\widetilde P_m\) satisfy \(\|\widetilde P_m-\widehat P_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta\).  Since \(\operatorname{tr}(\widehat P_m)\ge1\), some coordinate obeys \(\|\widehat P_me_j\|_2\ge1/\sqrt n\).  Choose a column of \(\widetilde P_m\) with maximal certified norm.  If \(\delta\le1/(8\sqrt n)\), its norm is at least \(7/(8\sqrt n)\).  Directed rational square-root and division enclosures produce a vector whose distance from the empirical range is at most \(3\sqrt n\,\delta\).  Denote the stacked, frame-mapped output by \(\widehat H_{\mathbb Q}\).  Repeating the normalization argument of (12) and stacking rows yields
\[
 \mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widehat H_{\mathbb Q},P)
 \le\frac{4\sqrt n\,e_{r_B}}{g_0}+8n\delta.
 \tag{36}
\]
If an outward rational frame is used for the ambient map, its operator contribution is added to the second term.  Choose all selector, normalization, and frame radii so that their total contribution is at most \(\tau/2\).  Equation (19) bounds the first term by \(\tau/7\), so (36) is strictly below \(\tau\).

Set every occurrence accuracy to the minimum specified after (28).  Equations (30), (34), and the inertia-bisection count show
\[
 p_{\mathrm{bit}}\le
 \operatorname{poly}\!\left(L,n,\log\kappa,
 \log(1/g_0),\log(1/h_0),\log(1/\alpha),\log(1/\tau)\right),
\]
where logarithms of reciprocals are truncated below at zero.  Indeed, \(\log(1/e_{\star})\) is bounded by the displayed logarithms and \(O(\log n+\log\kappa)\); on a nonempty promised class, \(g_0\le4\kappa^3\) controls the opposite scale.  Each restart has only \(Q=O(n^2)\) calls.  There are at most \(1+\log_2 B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) sampled stages, and the corrected definition makes \(\log B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) polynomial in the displayed logarithmic parameters.  Thus the complete post-summary Boolean cost has the asserted polynomial dependence.  Arithmetic intervals from a failed restart are discarded, so (29) is the relevant total for every transcript capable of returning.  Each finite rational call terminates.  The cap forces a final \(\bot\) on unresolved input, while on the event of probability at least \(1-\alpha\) from Theorem 1, (31)--(36) certify the correct graph and an encoder within \(\tau\) by \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}\).  Finally, if raw data rather than the covariance summaries are the input, merely reading the records costs \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\), before covariance formation; this proves the stated computational-scope qualification.
